items.body: San Gennaro; Gio Guido ジオ・グイド (guitar) Silvano Borzacchiello シルヴァーノ・ボルザッキエッロ (drums) Interviewed by Kenny Inaoka via cyber June/July, 2026 「サン・ジェンナーロ」は生粋のナポリタン・デュオ PART ONE: JazzTokyo： お二人はナポリのご出身だそうですが、現在はどちらに、どのくらいお住まいなのですか？ San Gennaro： はい、二人ともルーツはナポリにあります。シルヴァーノはスイスに住んでいて、私は2013年の4月から日本に住んでいます。 JT： お二人は、いつ、どこで出会ったのでしょう？ SG： 1992年にロサンゼルスのミュージシャンズ・インスティテュート（MI）です。 JT： 一緒に演奏するようになったのはいつ頃からですか？ SG： 出会ってからほんの数日後には、もう一緒に音を出していましたね。その後すぐに、同じくMIの学生だったベーシストのガイ・エレーズを交えて、ジャズ・ファンクのトリオを結成しました。 JT： デュオ名を「San Gennaro（サン・ジェンナーロ）」にした理由は？ SG： 数ヶ月前、電車の中でキース・ジャレットの『サンベア・コンサート』(ECM) を聴いていたんです。その日の夜、家に帰ってからシルヴァーノに電話をして、「日本ツアーに名前をつけよう」と提案しました。 私は「『サンベア・コンサート』みたいなやつさ……」と言おうとしたのですが、口から出たのは「『サン・ジェンナーロ』みたいなやつさ……」だったんです。私が言葉を続ける前に、シルヴァーノが話を遮って「それだ！サン・ジェンナーロにしよう！」と言ったんですよ。 最初は驚きました。普通なら、デュオやツアーの名前に宗教的な人物の名前を選ぶことはありませんからね。でも、よく考えてみたんです。私たちは二人ともナポリ出身ですし、ツアー日程の一つである9月19日は、ちょうど「サン・ジェンナーロの祝日」にあたります。それに、何より最初にパッと口から出た名前でもありました。 サン・ジェンナーロ（聖ジェンナーロ）とは； ナポリの守護聖人であり、ナポリの人々は加護を祈って彼に祈りを捧げます。そのため、9月19日はナポリにおいて非常に重要な祝祭の日なのです。 Silvano: それは、ジオからの１本の電話と提案によって瞬時に実現しました。理屈を超えた、導かれるような体験から生まれた自発的な展開でした。 そういったこともあって、「サン・ジェンナーロ」で行こう、ということになりました。 JT： 今回の日本ツアーは、どなたが企画・運営されているのですか？ SG： 私の会社である合同会社「Real Deal Music 」が主催しています。 JT： なぜ即興演奏をやろうと思われたのでしょう？これまでにも、デュオで即興演奏をしたことはあったのですか？ 「即時的作曲」を追求してきた Gio： 私にとって、これは現時点で到達した最高峰の音楽表現の形だと思っています —— とはいえ、これを単に「即興音楽」という言葉だけで片付けたくはありません。 私は長年、「即時的作曲（extemporaneous composition）」、つまり即興で演奏しながら曲を紡ぎ出していくというコンセプトを追究してきました。ミュージシャンとしての私の最大の挑戦は、メロディ、ハーモニー、形式、そして美しさを演奏の中心に据えながら、その瞬間に音楽を生み出していくことです。 もちろん、このアプローチは時として、アヴァンギャルド（前衛）やフリー・ジャズ特有の熱量や自由さへと向かうこともあります。しかし私にとって最も重要なのは、音楽そのものが持つ詩的で美しいアイデンティティなのです。 ギターとドラムによる、私たちの最初の完全な即興セッションは、2012年2月23日に行われました。場所は、当時私がイタリアのブスト・アルシーツィオに構えていたレコーディング・スタジオです。そのセッションが、私たちの初のリアルタイム作曲アルバム『Moment Now』となりました。 Silverno: 私たちはスタイルや音楽的感性の面で、常に自然と息が合っていました。お互いの道のりも、これまでごく自然に交わってきたのです。即興音楽のデュオCDを制作したこともありますし、このツアーを進めながら、今後もさらにCDを作っていきたいと考えています。 JT： キース・ジャレットの即興演奏にインスピレーションを受けているとのことですが、昨年（2025年）が『ケルン・コンサート』の50周年、そして今年（2026年）が日本で録音された『サンベア・コンサート』の50周年であることはご存じでしたか？ SG： ええ、もちろん知っています。『ケルン・コンサート』が1975年、『サンベア・コンサート』が1976年の録音ですね。キース・ジャレットのソロ・ピアノ・コンサート、そして彼の即興演奏に対するコンセプトや哲学からは、本当に大きなインスピレーションを受けてきました。 Silverno: その意味では、これが単なる偶然ではないと考えるのが自然でしょう。私たちは二人とも キース・ジャレットを愛しており、ここで挙げた２つのコンサートは、私たちの存在そのものに深く刻み込まれています。 ジャレットへのオマージュを捧げる、素晴らしい方法です。 JT： キースの即興演奏のアルバムの中で、特にどの作品が一番お好きですか？また、その理由も教えてください。 Gio： お気に入りのアルバムを一つだけ選ぶというのは、私にとって非常に難しいですね。 たとえば『サンベア・コンサート』には、即興で生まれたとは思えないほど美しい楽曲がいくつも収められています。中にはとても叙情的なものもあり、歌詞をつければそのまま美しい「歌」になってしまうのではないかと思えるほどです。 また、ミラノのスカラ座でのコンサート（『ラ・スカラ』）の冒頭を飾る楽曲も、信じられないほど素晴らしい。私にとってあのコンサートは、まるで一本の映画のサウンドトラックのようであり、もしそんな映画があるならば、間違いなくアカデミー作曲賞に値する名曲だと思っています。 『パリ・コンサート』のオープニングでは、バロック音楽の薫りが漂う美しい即興演奏から始まりますが、これもまた見事というほかありません。 そしてもちろん、『ケルン・コンサート』や『ウィーン・コンサート』、『ブレーメン・コンサート』などもあります。これらについても語り始めてしまうと、話がいくらあっても足りなくなってしまいます。ですから、やはり一つだけを選ぶのは難しいですね。 Silverno: 私にとっても、選ぶなんて不可能です。40年以上にわたり、トリオの音源やピアノ・ソロの録音をほぼ毎日聴き続けているのですから……。 JT： 今回の日本ツアーをライブ録音して、アルバムを制作される予定はありますか？ SG： はい。すべてが順調にいき、機材トラブルなどが起きなければ、ツアーの全公演をレコーディングする予定です。理想を言えば、各公演から1枚ずつ、計14枚のライブ・アルバムをお届けできればと考えています。 また、これらのコンサートのうち1公演だけ、他とは異なる編成で行う予定です。9月27日に大阪の「Jazz Club GALLON（ガロン）」で行うステージでは、フルート奏者の咲野ゆりさんを迎えてトリオとして演奏します。この日は、私のバンド「Airport」のオリジナル曲と即興演奏を織り交ぜてお届けする予定です。メロディ・ラインを奏でられる楽器が2つある状態で「即時的作曲（extemporaneous composition）」のコンセプトに挑むのは、非常に興味深い試みですし、より繊細なアプローチが求められることになるでしょう。 JT： Gio は、今回のツアーではアコースティックとエレキ・ギターの両方を弾く予定ですか？ Gio： はい、エレキ・ギターとナイロン弦のアコースティック・ギターの両方を使用します。 JT： シルヴァーノは、会場ごとに異なるドラムセットを叩くことになりますか？ Silverno：訪れる会場にはそれぞれ独自のドラムセットが用意されていますが、私はほぼ確実に、標準的なジャズ用の３ピース・キットにいくつかのスモール・パーカッションを加えて演奏する予定です。 JT： 使用される機材の仕様について教えていただけますか？ SG： 「サン・ジェンナーロ 日本ツアー2026」のすべてのパフォーマンスは、ポータブル仕様のプロ用レコーディング・システムを使用し、マルチトラックでライブ録音されます。 レコーディングのセットアップは、以下のような構成を予定しています。 レコーダー： Zoom H6 Essential（32bit float対応ポータブル・マルチトラック・レコーダー）。さらに拡張カプセル「EXH-6e」を使用し、XLR入力を計6チャンネルに拡張します。 ミキサー： ヤマハ（Yamaha）MG10XU アナログミキサー。ギターのシグナル管理とステレオのサブミックスに使用します。 アンプ： Spark GO（エレキ・ギターのシグナル用）。 エレキ・ギター： ギブソン（Gibson）137。Spark GOのステレオ出力から、ヤマハ MG10XUの5/6チャンネルへルーティングします。 アコースティック・ギター： アルハンブラ（Alhambra）CW 5P-E（ナイロン弦）。コンデンサーマイクと、楽器内蔵のピエゾピックアップの両方を使って録音します。 ドラム： 計4トラックで録音。ステレオペアのコンデンサーマイクをオーバーヘッド（天吊り）に配置し、さらにスネアドラムとキックドラムにそれぞれ近接（オンマイク）でセッティングします。 各コンサートは、高解像度のマルチトラックでキャプチャーされます。これにより、ツアー終了後にじっくりとミックスやマスタリングを行うことができ、ライヴ・コンサートならではの自発性、相互作用、そしてリアルタイムの創造性をそのまま作品に閉じ込めることが可能になります。 PART TWO JT： 音楽一家のお生まれですか？ Gio： はい。母はとても歌が上手でしたし、私の家族の近くにはいつも音楽がありました。７歳くらいの頃、いとこの多くがすでにギターを弾いていて、当時９歳だった私の兄もギターを始めました。私もそのすぐ後、８歳の時に彼らに続きました。 12歳の時には、姉、兄と私の３人でトリオを結成しました。主にビートルズの曲を演奏していたのですが、ビートルズのように全員で歌い、歌がとても上手だった姉がメイン・ボーカルを務めていました。 14歳の時、私たちは「The Reejoice」というロックバンドを結成しました。私がギター、兄がベース、姉がボーカルで、ドラマーもいました。オリジナル曲のアルバムをレコーディングし、いくつかのロック・フェスティバルにも出演しました。イタリアの音楽雑誌『Fare Musica』で紹介されたこともあります。その他にも、アーティスト兼画家の姉がもう一人いますし、弟は現在、プロのシンガー、ピアニスト、そしてキーボード奏者として活動しています。 Silverno： 父方も母方もミュージシャンの家系に生まれました。常に音楽が流れ、それが日常の一部になっているような環境でしたね。家族には詩人、作家、教師、そして複数の楽器をこなすマルチ奏者がいました。また、母はダンスが大好きで、そのコンテンポラリー・ダンスへの情熱を私に伝えてくれました。 JT： 最初に始めた楽器は何ですか？また、それはいつ頃ですか？ Guido：ギターです。8歳の時に弾き始めました。 Silverno：最初の楽器はクラリネットでした。地元の町のバンドで吹いていたのですが、すぐにドラムも始めて、そちらが私にとっての専門になりました。 すべての始まりは、10歳だった1974年のことです。 JT： ジャズや即興音楽との出会いはどうでしたか？ Gio：16歳の時、パット・メセニーを初めて聴いてからジャズを学び、練習し始めました。そのアルバムがパット・メセニー・グループの『トラヴェルズ』(ECM) です。あのアルバムが本当に大好きで、収録されているほぼすべての曲を習得し始めました。耳コピで採譜し、パット・メセニーのソロの多くを暗記したほどです。それが、私がジャズや即興演奏と本格的に向き合うようになった、まさに始まりでした。 Silverno：即興音楽には、スタイルに関係なく常に魅了されてきました。クラシックからロック、ジャズにいたるまで、ジャンルを超えた作曲家たちの間に、ある共通の糸――共通する道筋を見出したのです。その点において、フランク・ザッパは私のメンターでした。 JT： ナポリでは音楽の専門学校やジャズ・クラブ、ジャズ・フェスなどはどうですか？ Gio： ナポリとその周辺地域には、非常に豊かな音楽文化があります。アマルフィ海岸で開催される「ラヴェッロ・フェスティバル」、ポンペイ考古学公園の円形闘技場で開催される「ビーツ・オブ・ポンペイ」、そしてナポリ中心部で開催される「ナポリ・スウィング・フェスティバル」などがあります。 また、ジャズクラブもいくつかありますし、最も重要な音楽機関としては、イタリアの歴史ある音楽院の一つである「サン・ピエトロ・ア・マイエッラ音楽院」が挙げられます。 Silverno：いくつかあります。名前や場所は時代とともに変わっていきますが、世界の音楽史に膨大な楽曲を提供し、あらゆる場所のミュージシャンにインスピレーションを与えてきた街として、今でも重要な拠点であり続けています。特に「サン・ピエトロ・ア・マイエッラ」音楽院は、ジャズの学位やコースを取り入れています。 JT： プロとして音楽活動を始められたのはいつですか？ Gio：それは段階的なものでした。「The Reejoice」で演奏していた頃には、すでにプロとしてのコンサートをいくつかこなしていました。その後、私と兄はイタリアを離れることにしたのです。当時あった義務兵役によって、非常に重要な時期に自分たちの音楽活動の計画が中断されてしまうのを避けるためでした。 私たちは1987年にロンドンへ移住することで、合法的に兵役を回避しました。現地で定期的な仕事を見つけつつ、同時にミュージシャンたちと出会い、演奏し、ギグの仕事を得るようになっていきました。それが、イタリア国外における私のプロのミュージシャンとしてのキャリアの始まりでした。 Silverno：1985年にミラノで様々なバンドと演奏したのが、私の第一歩でした。当時のミラノは音楽活動が非常に盛んな時期で、ジャズやフュージョンが全盛期を迎えており、会場もたくさんありました。今では考えられないことですが、定期的なレギュラー出演（レジデンシー）もあったほどです。 私は個人レッスンで学んでいたため、ライヴ・パフォーマンスに割く時間がたっぷりとありました。当時演奏していたグループの一つに「Mob（モブ）」というバンドがあったのですが、当時はイタリアでも指折りの有名なジャズ・フュージョン・バンドの一つでした。 JT： アメリカでの音楽活動はいかがでしたか？ 「ザ・ジャズ・クルセーダーズ」のメンバーとして活躍 Gio： アメリカでの最初の音楽活動は、ドラムのシルヴァーノ・ボルザッキエッロ、ベースのガイ・エレズと組んでいたジャズ・ファンク・トリオでした。 また、ジャズ・シンガーとのデュオでも演奏していました。 その後「ザ・ジャズ・クルセイダーズ」 のウェイン・ヘンダーソンと出会いました。当時、彼は自身のアルバム『Sketches of Life』をプロデュースしているところでした。かいつまんで話すと、彼は私をスタジオに招き、彼の楽曲＜For Old Time’s Sake＞でギター・ソロを弾いてほしいと頼んできたのです。 その瞬間から、私は「ザ・ジャズ・クルセイダーズ」との仕事を始めました。彼らとの最初のコンサートは1993年5月のロングビーチ・ジャズ・フェスティバルでした。その後、1994年6月からはバンドのレギュラー・メンバーになりました。 Silverno： 当時の私の最優先事項はロサンゼルスのミュージシャンズ・インスティテュート（MI）に通うことでしたが、それでも様々な会場で演奏したり、合間にCMのスタジオ・ワークなどをこなしたりしていました。ジオと最初のバンドを結成したのも、ちょうどこの時期のことです。 JT：最も影響を受けたミュージシャンは誰ですか？ Gio：本当にたくさんいます。最初の大きな影響はパット・メセニーでした。その後、ジム・ホール、ウェス・モンゴメリー、ブランフォード・マルサリス、ジョージ・ベンソンといったミュージシャンたちの音楽を深く聴き込み、研究しました。また、バロック期から19世紀後半に至る偉大なクラシックの作曲家たちも挙げなければなりません。彼らの和声感覚、形式、旋律、そして感情の構築美は、私が音楽や作曲について考える上で深い影響を与えてくれました。 人生のこのステージにおいて、私に最も影響を与えているミュージシャンはキース・ジャレットです。音楽的な面だけでなく、彼の即興演奏に対する哲学、自発的な創造、そしてリアルタイムでの作曲というアプローチを通じて、多大な影響を受けています。 Silverno： 全員の名前を挙げるのは難しいですが、初期の段階で言えば、キース・ジャレット、マイケル・ブレッカー、ジャック・ディジョネット、ゲイリー・バートン、フランク・ザッパ、ハービー・ハンコック、ビル・エヴァンス、ジョン・コルトレーン、ウェス・モンゴメリー、ジョージ・デューク、パット・メセニー、ウェザー・リポート、バッハ、ベネデッティ・ミケランジェリ……本当に他にもたくさんいます。 JT： 最もお気に入りのアルバムを5枚挙げてもらえますか？ Gio： その質問に答えるのはいつも難しいのですが、あえて選ぶなら、以下の通りです。キース・ジャレット 『サンベア・コンサート』(ECM)、『ザ・ケルン・コンサート』(ECM) 、『ラ・スカラ』(ECM)、 パット・メセニー・グループ 『トラヴェルズ』(ECM) 、 ジム・ホール・トリオ 『ライヴ・イン・トロント 1975 』(A&M)。ギタリストとしては、特に『トラヴェルズ』とジム・ホールの『ライヴ・イン・トロント 1975』が、自分の成長において重要な作品でした。 JT： ジオ、いつ、なぜ日本へ移住したのですか？また、日本のミュージシャンと共演したことはありますか？ Gio：2013年4月に完全に移住する前にも、日本には何度か訪れたことがありました。 日本に来る前は、イタリア、ロンドン、リーズ（英）、パリ、ロサンゼルス、ニューヨークなど、さまざまな場所に住んでいました。それぞれの場所が、音楽的にも人間的にも、私に大切なものを与えてくれました。 しかし、日本は私にとても特別なものをもたらしてくれました。それは「平和（心の平穏）」です。 私にとって日本は、これまで暮らした中で最も平和で安全な国です。規律、敬意、責任感、そして社会の調和を重んじる日本文化のあり方を深くリスペクトしています。アーティストとして、その穏やかな環境のおかげで、音楽と創造性に深く集中することができるのです。 ここに移住してからは多くの日本のミュージシャンと共演してきました。長年にわたり日本で精力的に活動しており、自身のジャズ・ファンク・バンド「Airport」をはじめとする様々なプロジェクトでの演奏や、多くの素晴らしい日本のミュージシャンとのコラボレーションを行っています。こちらで築き上げてきた音楽的なつながりには、本当に感謝しています。 JT： 自身のおすすめのアルバムを教えてください。 Gio： 私自身のアルバムの中からでしたら、『Extemporaneous Compositions』をおすすめします。このアルバムは、2025年12月14日から2026年2月17日にかけて行われた数回のYouTubeライブ配信中に、ライヴ録音されたものです。どの楽曲もリアルタイムに、つまり事前の譜面や用意を一切排し、即興演奏をしながらその場で作曲されました。 私にとってこのアルバムは、現在の自分の音楽的な方向性を最も明確に示している作品の一つです。単なるフリー・インプロヴィゼーション（自由即興）ではなく、メロディ、ハーモニー、形式、そして感情を演奏の中心に据えながら、その瞬間に「完成された楽曲」を作り上げようという試みです。 その意味で、『Extemporaneous Compositions』は、シルヴァーノと私が行う「サン・ジェンナーロ ・ジャパン・ツアー 2026」でのアプローチとも深くつながっています。その瞬間に生まれつつも、作曲の意図を持って形作られていく音楽です。 以下が試聴リンクです： プレイリストはこちらです； https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I926I-5ye64&list=PLQn6O6NIgrZ7T8K_pyzbi6EVaHgx0JIKN JT： 最後に、それぞれの夢を語ってください。 Gio： 私の夢は、「サン・ジェンナーロ・ ジャパン・ツアー 2026」が人々の記憶に残るものになることです。単なる一連のコンサートではなく、ジャズや音楽のコミュニティに意味のある足跡を残すような音楽体験にしたいと考えています。 このツアーを通じて、リアルタイム・コンポジション（即興作曲）の持つ力――誠実さ、美しさ、リスク、そして深い対話とともに、その瞬間に紡ぎ出される音楽の力を示すことができればと願っています。 Silverno： 夢はすでに私たちの日常生活の中にあります。演奏し、自分たちが感じていることをできる限り誠実に表現するチャンスが与えられていること。そして今回、様々な理由から二人とも大好きな国である日本が、この続きゆく夢に新たな１ページを贈ってくれること……それが夢そのものです。 ♫ サン・ジャンナーロ・ジャパン・ツアー 2026 https://jazztokyo.org/news/post-123146/
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由吉他手乔·吉多与鼓手西尔瓦诺·博尔扎基耶洛组成的拿坡里二重奏专辑，以完全即兴演奏为核心，两位音乐人自1992年在洛杉矶MI相识以来长期合作。专辑延续了他们自2012年首次完全即兴录音以来的创作路线，强调"即时作曲"概念，在自由爵士的热量与抒情美感之间寻求平衡。专辑名称源自拿坡里守护圣人圣杰纳罗的节日，呼应了Keith Jarrett《Sun Bear Concert》的命名逻辑，并直接受到其即兴哲学的深刻影响。整体演奏追求在无预设框架中构建旋律、和声与形式的美学统一，而非纯粹的前卫噪音。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — When Crimso took the road without Ade and Broof , little did we know that this period would be thelonguest +/- uninterrupted chapter of the band, also the last one and furthemore embodying all oftheir career. I'd seen the Thrak double trio tours twice and was a little disappointed that Frippwas still shunning most of the 70's body of works, except for some Red Aspic tracks and the oddSchizoid encore. I had also shunned the Light and Power album tours as well, but this three drummerline-up was celebrating the full Crimson legacy, so I caught them three times over the 7 or 8 yearsof this phase. TBH, I first had to listen to the Orpheum release (borrowed from a buddy), and I wasn't all thatconvinced by the track list and Jakko's voice wasn't convincing me to go and witness another concertof theirs. Indeed, despite some Island tracks on the list, something was missing from thisperformance (other than Jakko's renditions), but also that it wasn't a full concert,, timing barelyabouve 80 minutes. Of course the band would go on to much better things and I never regretted thethree concerts witnessed between '17 and '20.Owning three 3-drummers line-up album (Toronto, Radical Action & Chicago), there is no way Orpheumcan compete in terms of essential late-era live album, so I'd tell you to avoid this one, but thatwould not do justice to the music on it, despite its few flaws. Hence three stars.
items._genre: eclectic prog / progressive rock / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评围绕King Crimson三鼓手时期在Orpheum的现场演出展开。作者回顾了乐队自Thrak以来的现场演变，指出这套阵容是乐队历史上持续时间最长、最完整演绎其音乐遗产的阶段。演出时长约80分钟，收录曲目涵盖了乐队不同时期的作品，但作者认为新主唱Jakko的演绎未能完全传达原作精髓，且曲单编排不够完整。相比于Toronto、Radical Action等其他三鼓手时期现场专辑，Orpheum在曲目精华度和整体表现上略逊一筹。作者给出三星评价，既肯定了演出本身的音乐水准，也诚实指出了与其他现场录音相比的不足之处，适合想了解该时期演出的乐迷作为补充收藏。

items.body: Francis Buseko looks at the brilliant diaristic album completed in the face of tragedy which, while once mired in controversy, now is clearly the work of a coherent artistic vision One of the tragedies of Yoko Ono’s career is that she has so often been treated as a symbol before being taken seriously as an artist in her own right. Season Of Glass arrived at the moment when that symbolic weight threatened to become permanent. Released just seven months after the murder of John Lennon, Ono’s fifth studio album appeared at a time when the world seemed ready to define her forever through loss: as widow, survivor, keeper of memory. Instead, she does something characteristically Yoko Ono: she creates art... The post Reissue of the Week: Yoko Ono’s Season Of Glass appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 《Season of Glass》是小野洋子在约翰·列侬遇刺后七个月发行的第五张录音室专辑，将私人悲剧转化为连贯的艺术表达。评论聚焦于小野长期被符号化、被视为'遗孀'而非独立艺术家的困境，指出这张专辑正是她以日记式创作直面痛苦的回应。唱片以极端情感暴露为核心，延续了她一贯的概念艺术路线——声音碎片、极简重复、环境音景与呼喊交织，拒绝以传统歌曲结构安抚听众。乐评将其视为小野艺术理念的一次清晰呈现，而非一时情绪的宣泄。专辑承载了私人记忆的重量，同时也预示了后来她在噪音、氛围与实验音乐领域的持续探索。整体听感沉重而内省，录音中保留了列侬生前相关的声音片段，使作品成为一份无法被简单归类的艺术文献。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — After the nearly-perfect Latin-infused Jazz-Rock Fusion debut album of the previous year, the Wilson Brothers' band continued touring and polishing their sound while also fine-tuning their vision of where they wanted to go (how their music would evolve). Mandrill Is was released by Polydor Records one year to the date after the release of the debut album: April 1, 1972.1. "Ape Is High" (5:36) the immediate feel I get from the first few seconds of this song is that the band is trying to ride on the coattails of RARE EARTH's massively popular hit from the previous year entitled, "I Just Want to Celebrate"--and this feeling sustains itself with its whole-group choir chant-singing and JoeWalsh-like guitar strumming from rhythm guitarist Omar Mesa (who's solo/lead work later in the song is quite good). The horns suddenly appear in the second minute, providing accents to the vocal lines in the chorus. Kofi Cave's Hammond organ play becomes more prominent in the third minute, culminating in a nice solo in the fourth before Omar's guitar turns standard Rock. Nice finish. I can't help but rate this upward due to the tight arrangements and performances. (8.875/10)2. "Cohelo" (1:45) a gentle Latin groove that is led by Ric Wilson's flute and backed by the "What's Going On"-like party sounds and emerging "Co-HE-lo" vocals going on in the background. I love it! (5/5)3. "Git It All" (4:30) another song that feels as if it was contrived to come from a White man's Rock perspective (which feels somewhat false and pretentious to these musicians) as the bass line, guitar-and-organ chord and sound choices as well as the foundational drum pattern feel so watered down for the arousal of primordial martial aggression. The rest of the band--and especially the party choir--feel as if they're into it but there is little of the band members' Panamanian roots coming through in this music (not even from the horn section); it all feels affected, adaptational, and manufactured. (8.75/10)4. "Children of the Sun" (4:57) flute and zither-like chord strokes open this awesome song, covering nearly the full first two minutes before bursting into a flurry of dynamic Jazz-Rock. But then everything calms down after the burst into a gentle melodic fare with soft vocals for about 90-seconds before the Afro-Cubano/Salsa horns shake everything up with some wake-up bursts of sound--which results in the incitement of the rest of the musicians to step it up a couple of notches. The result is some of the coolest Latin-Jazz-Rock you're likely to ever hear! But, alas! it doesn't last! The deep vocals return (within the Salsa party music) and then come to an end very shortly thereafter. A strange but ultimately impressive (and gutsy/ingenious) song. (9.5/10) 5. "I Refuse to Smile" (4:06) a pretty song that is styled like a combination of MARVIN GAYE's What's Going On fare and other Motown (The Temptations) sounds. The musicianship is so impressive! (The vocals a little less so.) (8.875/10)6. "Universal Rhythms" (3:23) a "song" that opens with a minute of typical conversation between two young children (one older and bossier, the other younger and less experienced). It is then interrupted by the appearance of "The Enchanting Wizard" to tell the children about the "rhythms of the Universe." Colors, dreams, truth, emotion, sound, past, present, and tomorrow, peace. Aquarian evangelsim and nourishment. 7. "Lord of the Golden Baboon" (3:34) a jam founded in funk-rock but expanded by the array of Afro-Latin percussion instruments and Latin melody and chord progressions and, later, punctuating accents of the horn section. Though still a little SANTANA-inspired, the band is starting to make it their own. (9.125/10) 8. "Central Park" (4:06) sounding like it comes from an Off-Broadway hippie-consciousness-raising musical like Hair or Godspell as well as a little of Chicago and Blood, Sweat & Tears. The instrumental section that starts at 2:45 is so like CHICAGO but the orchestra strings and vocal keep it anchored on the stage of musicals. As a show-tune it really works! (9/10)9. "Kofijahm" (3:38) the album's second composition from keyboard maestro Clause "Coffee" Cave is a true tribute to the airy Caribbean music that celebrates its population's African roots. Now, this is a true Latin-oriented expression of the spirit of Jazz-Rock Fusion. (9.75/10) 10. "Here Today Gone Tomorrow" (4:18) a song based on a four chord cycle of power chords that sounds as if it were coming from a Rock 'n' Roll band like Cream, Grand Funk Railroad, or Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young, it is peppered with nice/tension-relieving bridges of gentle flute and xylophone but overall its really a rocker. It's even got the wordless female vocals to back up the aggressive lead vocalist. (8.75/10)11. "The Sun Must Go Down" (3:25) wind, gentle and spacious guitar chords with a mellifluous male vocal singing over the top, the song sounds, and continues to sound, like another Off-Broadway expression of mantras and colloquialisms of the Aquarian Age's hippie-speak. It is, however, a good, solid song no matter its orientation. (9/10)Total Time 43:18Unfortunately, the band has chosen a more lively, live-performance-friendly WAR-like direction for its musical direction. It's all very skillful and polished as well as being very conducive to vociferous audience participation, but it is, to my mind and ears, no longer befitting the categorization of Jazz-Rock Fusion (but still qualifying for the Jazz-Rock micro-genre). (I blame the loss of original bass player Bundie Cenas, being replaced by Frederick "Fudgie Kae" Solomon, as the core reason for the change in the band's foundational sound.)A/five stars; though not a Jazz-Rock Fusion album, this eclectic mix of styles is presented in such a well-composed and beautifully-performed fashion that I cannot deny it its masterpiece recognition. As a whole, however, I would happily and willingly admit Mandril Is into the micro-genre of Jazz-Rock music. I just want the band to feel more free and compelled to express themselves more naturally--from the Afro-Cubano music of their Panamanian roots.
items._genre: jazz-rock fusion / latin fusion / world fusion
items._cn_summary: Mandrill的第二张专辑延续了首作拉丁爵士摇滚的路线，乐队成员拥有巴拿马裔背景，试图在白人摇滚语汇与拉丁传统之间寻找平衡。专辑中Hammond风琴、萨克斯管与电吉他交织，配合打击乐构建层次丰富的律动。部分曲目如《Children of the Sun》展现了从原声序奏到萨尔萨爆发再到爵士摇滚过渡的动态编排，体现出乐队对拉丁爵士融合的深入探索。然而评论者也指出，某些曲目（如《Git It All》）的摇滚段落显得做作而缺乏文化根源，流于表面的白人摇滚模仿削弱了作品的独特性。整体而言，这是一张在融合方向上有想法但执行尚不够纯粹的拉丁爵士摇滚作品，与当代实验音乐的距离仍然较大，但其中暗含的世界音乐视角值得关注。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — German/European music legend Michael Naura is back after his bout with polyserositis--and he's picked up the Fender Rhodes electric piano. The album was recorded in 1970 and released either late in 1970 or early in 1971.A1. "Soledad De Murcia" (5:57) like most of the songs on this album this one starts out and continues to develop as if it's a cover of some other familiar pop song ("Hurts so Good") with some really cool STEVE JANSEN-like drumming, but it's not: like all of the songs on this album, this is supposedly an original composition from band leader Michael Naura. At the same time it makes for one of the amazingly soothing/comforting songs that help make this album so dear to me. The interplay of the four musicians is so warm and supportive--and yet creative and professional. Drummer Joe Nay is especially impressive as is bandleader/composer Michael Naura's generosity in giving so much shine to the other three musicians (while taking very little for himself). Yet the rich, thick vibrato of his electric piano provides all of the comfort and support necessary for his band mates to fly. And I love how we're hearing the beginnings of Eberhard Weber's fluid "underwater" sound coming from his bass playing. I love it! (9.75/10)A2. "M.O.C." (3:37) upbeat and uptempo feel good danceable jazz with some great, active threads woven together from all four musicians. This one is more impressive for its individual performances fitting so well together into one weave without all of the nostalgic warmth of the opener. (9.125/10) A3. "Forgotten Garden" (5:53) slow and steady, everything is spaced so far apart and yet the long-held notes reverberating from the Rhodes, Wolfgang's vibraphone, Eberhard's tonally-fluid bass, and even Joe Nay's delicate cymbal play. The main star, of course, is Wolfgan Schl�ter, but it's the complete sonosphere of the whole that really carries me off to other worlds! Beautiful! And so serene. (9.25/10)A4. "Take Us Down To The River" (3:58) a saturated sound palette that will eventually become derided for its posh hippy associations, I can't help but think of this as fresh and refreshing even now, 55+ years after the Fender Rhodes, electric bass, and vibraphone made their way into jazz and pop music. A little cheesy, yes, but still forward-thinking for its time. (8.875/10)B1. "Why Is Mary So Nervous?" (5:28) an interesting song for the two different rhythm speeds the band moves back and forth between; it really does convey the kind of inconsistency that denotes nervousness. Nice drum solo from Joe in the fourth minute. Overall I think it a little odd, even weird, but definitely interesting--and well-performed with the final minute being the best of it. (9/10)B2. "Don't Stop" (4:56) this one feels like a hard bop/blues-rock cover of a classic tune. Both Joe and Eberhard really shine on this one despite Michael and Wolfgang's command of the spotlight. (8.875/10)B3. "Miriam" (11:05) dreamy, impressionistic, mostly vibraphone, Fender Rhodes, and bass interplay that, I have to say it, sounds a lot like some of the background music I used to hear on Mr. Rogers' Neighborhood back in the day--which is meant as no disrespect to the great jazz pianist Johnny Costa that Fred Rogers employed as music director for his show. My comment is only meant to note from where my feeling of "familiarity" comes. There are some nice solos given (and taken) by Eberhard (in the eighth and ninth minutes) as well as to Joe--plus the shut-down at the nine-minute mark to finish is really cool. (17.5/20)B4. "Call" (5:03) like most of the songs on this album this one starts out and continues to develop as if it's a cover of some other familiar pop song, but it's not: like all of the songs on this album, this is supposedly an original composition from band leader Michael Naura--and it may just be the best, most cohesive whole-band collaboration on the album. Wolfgang Schl�ter is remarkable on the vibraphone, Michael really engaged with his Rhodes support, and Eberhard and Joe seem so relaxed into the groove: it's as if they're all totally entrained to the groove. (9.125/10)Total time: 39:00A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of wonderful Rhodes-and-vibe-driven Jazz-Rock Fusion.

items._cn_summary: 1970年录制的德国爵士融合专辑，Michael Naura四重奏以Rhodes电钢琴为核心，结合颤音琴、电贝斯与爵士鼓构建出温暖而富有空间的声响。整张专辑以原创作品为主，风格偏向柔和的即兴爵士融合，乐手之间的互动默契被反复强调。评论者特别赞赏Eberhard Weber早期流畅的贝斯音色以及Joe Nay细腻的鼓点处理，并将Schlüter的颤音琴视为亮点之一。部分曲目带有当时的放克与硬波普色彩，整体氛围宁静而具沉思性，但并未走向极端实验或前卫领域。专辑作为欧洲爵士融合早期录音具有一定的历史价值，适合对早期电声爵士融合感兴趣的听众。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Bl� Som Altid" ("Blue as Always") is the fourth full-length studio album by Danish progressive rockact Ache. The album was released through the KMF label in 1977. As of now (July 2026) the album hasnot seen a reissue, and therefore only the original vinyl and cassette tape versions from 1977exist. "Bl� Som Altid" is the follow-up release to "Pictures From Cyclus 7" from May 1976 and therehave been a couple of lineup changes since the last album as lead vocalist Stig Kreutzfeldt has left(he would soon form the commercially successful Rugsted/Kreutzfeldt pop/rock band) and foundingmember and keyboard player Peter Mellin has also jumped ship. Kreutzfeldt has not been replaced asAche already had two lead vocalists in the lineup and Johnnie Gellett therefore just stepped up andperformed all lead vocals on "Bl� Som Altid". Mellin has been replaced by Per Wium. Wium came fromCV J�rgensen�s band where he had played with drummer Gert Smedegaard.Stylistically "Bl� Som Altid" follows a similar yet less mainstream seeking progressive rock soundas Ache introduced on "Pictures From Cyclus 7". Funk, jazz-rock, folk, and progressive rock elementsare combined with a few more mainstream leaning AOR elements, although "Bl� Som Altid" is asmentioned leaning less in that direction and more in a progressive rock direction. The mostsignificant change since the last album is that Ache have now opted to sing in their native languageinstead of performing English language lyrics and it works really well for them. I�m slightlyreminded of Atlas' "Bl� Vardag" album from 1979, which of course is a fully instrumental release,but there are some similarities which make me think of that album.Upon conclusion "Bl� Som Altid" is a wonderful Danish language progressive rock release and arguablyone of the best quality Danish language progressive rock albums from the 1970s. It�s dynamic,varied, and well performed by a unit of skilled musicians. The songwriting is intriguing andengaging, and the icing on the cake is the organic, detailed, and well sounding production job. Ahigh quality release through and through. A 3.5 star (70%) rating is deserved.

items._cn_summary: 这张1977年丹麦乐队Ache的第四张录音室专辑呈现出融合放克、爵士摇滚、民谣与前卫摇滚的混合风格，并加入少量偏主流的AOR元素。乐队经历人事变动后，放弃了英语歌词，转而以母语丹麦语演唱，这一调整为作品增添了独特的地方文化色彩。评论者将其与Atlas 1979年的器乐专辑《Blå Vardag》相提并论，认为二者在气质上有相通之处。专辑在制作上保持了有机而细腻的质感，动态丰富且编排用心，被视为七十年代丹麦语前卫摇滚中品质最高的作品之一。然而，该评论的整体取向仍偏向传统前卫摇滚范畴内的品质认可，对于追求更极端实验性、即兴自由或电子解构的听众来说，融合度与突破性略显有限。

items.body: Soft Cell’s “In Heaven (When I Dance With You)” comes striding out of Danceteria with a lipstick grin and enough downtown perfume to turn the subway into its own discotheque. Marc Almond sings as though the dance floor has waited forty-seven years for him, while the late, great Dave Ball built the track from buoyant keyboards, clipped percussion, and bass that nudges the hips toward misbehaviour. The tune feels immediate, polished, and full of the odd angles that have always made Soft Cell excellent party hosts. “Soft Cell have always had a strong connection with New York, and my Soft Cell lyrics often look at America through British eyes,” says Almond. “New York in the 1980s was a particularly creative place for me. It was a pivotal era in terms of changes in my personal life and changes in the city itself. New York shaped Soft Cell, as it opened up a whole new world of possibilities. It was dirty, dark and dangerous – a real Wild West – but it was also deeply inspiring and exciting. A lot of our original influences came from America anyway: New York punk, Devo, Suicide, Lou Reed, disco and 1960s soul. But New York was like nowhere else on earth. There were 24-hour nightclubs, music, art and underground theatre. It offered a cornucopia of energy and edge, and the lyrics on ‘Danceteria’ reflect that time of my life.” That biography lives inside the record; a museum tag would only get in the way. Ball’s arrangement keeps changing the room by inches: a bright keyboard figure, a sly rhythmic turn, then a chorus broad enough for strangers to become temporary relatives. Almond works the lyric with the seasoned theatricality of someone who knows sincerity can wear eyeliner and still mean every word. His delivery carries delight, appetite, and the suspicion that somebody has already stolen your coat. “In Heaven (When I Dance With You) is a celebration of the early ’80s joyful disco scene,” says Almond. “A coming together of the sentiments of the time. I wanted it to be that moment when you run to the dance floor.” Almond gets his wish; the single finds disco’s social velocity: private feeling becomes public motion, and nobody needs to fill out a form. Its summer brightness carries a small ache because the track belongs to Ball’s farewell, completed two days before his death. That knowledge adds weight, yet the music keeps moving with generosity and comic grace; even grief is asked to check its shoes at the floor’s edge. As a preview of Soft Cell’s final album, In Heaven (When I Dance With You) makes a persuasive invitation. It remembers a New York of clubs, art kids, queer communion, bad decisions, and excellent shoes, then converts memory into present-tense pleasure. Ball’s production remains precise and playful; Almond gives the melody a grin wide enough to smuggle history through customs. Soft Cell leave the party as they entered it: with machines humming, hearts exposed, and somebody in the corner wondering whether dawn is really necessary. Listen below: Due September 25th 2026, via Republic of Music, Danceteria will be released on vinyl and CD, with the CD edition expanded to 14 tracks through the bonus cuts Crackland and What Is Your Morality. Listen to In Heaven (When I Dance With You) below and order it here. You can pre-order Danceteria here. items.body: When the Rolling Stones recorded “(I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction” in 1965, dissatisfaction came crackling through transistor radios amid advertising pitches, postwar consumer plenty, sexual frustration, and the suspicion that modern life was selling desires it could never fulfill. But what if the song were written now? It very well might confront a stranger predicament: every conceivable choice within reach, every connection replaceable, and the growing fear that access to anything and everything has left us satisfied by almost nothing. Brooklyn-based artist Black Marble answers that “What If?” with Anything, carrying the old complaint into an era of endless options and easy exits. Anything begins with a clipped guitar figure that could have slipped out of a college station at 2 a.m., back when radio still felt like a clubhouse run by sleep-deprived obsessives with bad posture and excellent record collections. Chris Stewart has spent fourteen years making pop music with machines that hum, wobble, and occasionally seem ready to electrocute the landlord, yet this track carries a springy immediacy, a small-room bounce built from dry drums, chiming guitar, and keyboards that hover at the edge of the frame. You can hear the dust on the knobs, which is far more persuasive than another immaculate digital coffin. The tune moves fast enough to suggest pleasure, while Stewart’s voice drifts through it with the calm of a man discovering that every available exit leads to another room full of way too many possibilities. The new guitar emphasis gives Black Marble a leaner body. Pylon and Wire hover nearby as useful ancestors, though Stewart avoids museum polish. The instruments feel handled, bumped, and left with fingerprints. “I want to dream us up. I’ll do anything, but it’s not enough!” This line lands with the blunt embarrassment of admitting that abundance can feel like starvation. Everybody has options, everybody has a profile, everybody can vanish before breakfast, and somehow the modern romance has become a customer-service portal where nobody can find the button marked “human being.” “Anything is basically a bedroom pop version of Satisfaction but it trades the carnal undertones for more of a domestic pastiche,” says Stewart. “…the center of the struggle is less about finding temporary satisfaction, but that today’s glut of options and opportunities gives every relationship an expiration date, every encounter an easy off ramp and every minor annoyance a reason to move on. The sentiment is the same from those old days, lack of fulfillment, but it’s due to modern circumstances. It feels like we have every option at our fingertips but we’re somehow losing the ability to connect.” Stewart follows the idea into the apartment, where resentment breeds beside the open window and friendship keeps showing up unannounced. His revolution is domestic, cramped, and slightly ridiculous, which makes it believable. Mick Jagger wanted release; Stewart sounds trapped inside the endless menu, scrolling past intimacy until the screen goes dim. Scott Kiernan’s video, shot at Various/Artists in New York City, converts that unease into visual overload. Images pile up with the appetite of a browser containing forty tabs, while Stewart remains meditative at the center, present yet swallowed by the barrage. The clip makes overstimulation feel comic and exhausting, a public carnival staged around private disconnection. Watch Anything below: Anything is pop for people who suspect convenience has made them lonelier. Its hook smiles with one side of its mouth, its rhythm keeps moving, and its central ache stays lodged beneath the floorboards. Stewart has made a fine little machine for dancing around the knowledge that freedom, multiplied without limit, can become another form of confinement. Listen to Anything below. items.body:
Tricky's most confident full-length since the 1990s, 'Different When It's Silent' is a dark, painful and melancholy reflection on decades spent in the spotlight and the tragic death of his daughter.

Tricky was never particularly chuffed with the term "trip-hop". Even back in the '90s he bristled at its mention, telling Melody Maker he'd "fucking deny having anything to do with it." And since then he's preferred to stake his claim as a perpetual outsider, jokingly calling his music "Tricky-hop" instead. But you can't deny his influence on the genre: here's an artist who was working with legendary Bristolian sound system the Wild Bunch before he was out of school and joined Massive Attack when he was still a teen, all this before going on to pen one of the genre's core texts. Even as the '90s drew to a close, trip-hop's oily early essence had been swapped out for the relative candyfloss of Morcheeba, Sneaker Pimps and Zero 7. And now, the genre's a catchall term - used to describe Eartheater, Erika de Casier, James K... even FKA twigs. You probably see why Tricky was so reticent to take the label seriously.

Because in 2026, trip-hop's meaning has shifted but Tricky really hasn't. He's still working with roughly the same elements, projecting his will into tracks that sound as if they're trapped between rocks and hard places from across the musical quarry: metal, rap, dub, industrial music. You'll notice a conspicuous absence of lounge or acid jazz. "Make me wanna die," groans vocalist Mitch Sanders on the opening track, echoing Martina Toppley Bird's delivery on the 'Pre-Millennium Tension' masterpiece. Sanders is a new voice for Tricky, but comes from familiar soil, the Bristol-born son of one of his closest friends. And he's a good conduit for Tricky's emotions. Starting with a callback to his most crucial material, Tricky is making a connection that holds up, too - 'Different When It's Silent' sounds like the Tricky album many of us were expecting to appear in the wake of 'Angels With Dirty Faces'.

It's an album of songs, not just ideas, and Tricky's hoarse voice is there like an omnipresent force in the background, growling next to Sanders' own. On 'Be Still in the Pain' he falls into a ghostly falsetto that fills the top end next to Tricky's wormy analog synth bass and skippy beat, but it's Run Red Rambo, another Bristol talent who helps tie this one together, laying down a rap that perfectly contrasts the other two vocals. And Tricky's hooks still hit hard when they need to - the tear-inducing chorus on 'Paris Maybe' or the druggy callback to a world before Britpop on 'I'm Yours'. And it all comes to a head on the finale, when Tricky brings back Polish singer Marta Złakowska for a track that directly addresses the death of his daughter in 2019. "It's a great way to end the album," he explains in the accompanying press release. "And then I can move on to other things."
items._cn_summary: Tricky的新专辑被视为其自1990年代以来最自信的完整作品，是一段关于几十年舞台生涯与女儿逝世的黑暗、痛苦而忧郁的沉思。专辑延续了他对trip-hop标签的抵触，坚持将自身定位为局外人。音乐风格横跨金属、说唱、dub与工业，刻意回避lounge和acid jazz等元素。新人Mitch Sanders粗粝的声线与Tricky沙哑的人声交织，Bristol本土说唱歌手Run Red Rambo的加入丰富了层次。模拟合成器贝斯线与跳动的鼓点构建出压迫性的声场，'Paris Maybe'的催泪副歌和'I'm Yours'对Britpop前夜的迷幻回望显示出Tricky依然锋利的旋律直觉。终曲与波兰歌手Marta Złakowska的合作直接面对2019年女儿离世的主题，以私人化的悲痛作为专辑的告别与释怀。整体而言，这是一张植根于Bristol声音传统却拒绝被归类的作品。

items.body:
Helado Tropical, the debut collaborative album from Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical.

"It didn’t begin with a plan so much as a meeting: two artists orbiting similar questions around language, identity, and music, finally landing in the same room. What followed was less a traditional writing process than a shared unfolding – an instinctive, immersive exchange that stretched across geographies, time zones, and states of being.

The duo first met in June 2024 in North Carolina, brought together by a mutual friend and a loose invitation to spend time in the studio. What might have been a brief session turned into something closer to a three-day sleepover – equal parts conversation, curiosity, and creative risk. Reyna Tropical, accustomed to close-knit collaborations, stepped into new creative territory, while Helado Negro brought a similar sense of curiosity and fluidity.

What emerged was immediate, rather than easing into collaboration, the two found themselves propelled forward by it – building songs in real time, responding to each other’s instincts without over-explaining them. There was no rigid division of roles. One would begin an idea, the other would answer. A melody would suggest a rhythm; a rhythm would reshape a lyric.

Across Helado Tropical, there is a noticeable absence of constraint: not just musically, but conceptually. Both artists share a long-standing resistance to the expectations often placed on Latin music: what it should sound like, how it should feel, what stories it should tell. As they do individually, these two artists create space for something more fluid and personal on this project.

What makes Helado Tropical particularly resonant is the sense of trust that underpins it. Trust in each other, of course, but also trust in instinct and in the process. Much of the album was written through improvisation, with meaning revealing itself only later, as the artists listened back and reflected."

items._cn_summary: 这是Helado Negro与Reyna Tropical的首张合作专辑，起源于两人2024年在北卡罗来纳州的一次偶然录音室会面，演变为为期三天的即兴创作。整张专辑以即兴方式构建，没有严格分工，一人抛出想法另一人即时回应，旋律引出节奏，节奏重塑歌词。两位艺术家都拒绝拉丁音乐的传统期待，试图创造更具流动性与个人化的表达空间。信任与直觉是这张专辑的核心——许多歌曲通过即兴写作完成，意义在事后回听时才逐渐显现。专辑呈现出一种跨地域、跨时区的创作状态融合，强调过程本身而非结果，概念上对拉丁音乐既有类型的边界进行了松绑。

items.body:
Strong new doublepack from Short Span’s increasingly prolific Natal Zaks aka Picture, following his excellent ‘Eeeeeeee’ label debut with a new set of driving, swinging specials, tipped FFO Convextion, Plastikman, Shinichi Atobe, Miles Demdike.

‘Uuuuuuuu’ follows suit from ‘Eeeeeeee’ with six distinctively brisk, detailed and aerated swingers ranging from crispy, tracky jack-tracks to friskier chord riders well poised for various points of the night. The mesmerising whisk of ‘Quuuuuuu’ sets up a dead strong suite taking in swingeing techno-house on ‘Ruuuuu’, and Brinkmann-meets-Grungerman hypnosis of ‘Miiiiiii’, whilst the frothing ‘Leeeeeee’ gets right under the skin like some Shinichi Atobe-meets-Convextion special for Chain Reaction, and the hardgroovers get served with friskiest shake of ‘Wooooooo’.

Yyyyyyyyy is also on the way, collect them all!
items._cn_summary: Picture（本名Natal Zaks）的第二张发行延续了其首张作品的气质，推出六首节奏驱动的电子舞曲。整张专辑以干脆利落的摇摆节拍和通透的空间感为核心，从清脆的jack节拍曲目到更灵活的弦律推进器，覆盖夜晚不同时段的DJ需求。'Quuuuuuu'以迷幻的扫频音效铺陈开篇，'Ruuuuu'呈现厚重的techno-house律动，'Miiiiiii'带有Brinkmann式的催眠质感，'Leeeeeee'则展现了类似Chain Reaction厂牌出品的深沉层次，而'Wooooooo'为偏爱硬派techno的听众提供了更激烈的选择。评论明确将其置于Convextion、Plastikman、Shinichi Atobe等minimal techno名家的谱系之中，整体属于地下电子舞曲范畴，注重细节打磨与功能性平衡。

items.body:
A second pressing of last year’s gorgeous fourth and final album from Old Saw, the American Primitive project of Tongue Depressor's Henry Birdsey, riffing on the classic Takoma paradigm with additional ferric washes and layered instrumental drones, huge recommendation if yr into Bruce Langhorne’s ‘The Hired Hand’ or classic work by Daniel Lanois, Laraaji, Pelt, Stars Of The Lid, State River Widening.

'The Wringing Cloth' is Birdsey’s fourth and final Old Saw outing, and ironically it’s also the one that has garnered most amount of critical and commercial success. Old Saw’s shimmering, drone-heavy soundscapes were recorded on 1/4" tape at various locations in New England over the last few years and are once again paired with evocative black and white imagery from photographer Dylan Hausthor, whose landscapes somehow perfectly capture the timeless, widescreen appeal of the music inside.

Birdsey's pedal, lap steel and resonator are at the core of each track, but the album also features Old Saw’s usual personnel; Harper Reed on nylon string guitar and banjo, Ira Dorset on fiddle and bowed strings, Ann Rowlis on reed organ and harmonium, Jim Cutler on telecaster, Addison Starkweather-Price on bass, and Peter Catchpole on metal objects and power hammer. That lap steel lends the music its stylistic anchor, taking us through decades of American folk before gently fraying at the edges. Birdsey's application of classical minimalism - the themes that surge through his work with Zach Rowden as Tongue Depressor - is still somehow present here, especially as the record pulls into its second side and the shimmering country-fied atmosphere is pierced with bell-like sounds, but the overall mood and flavour of the record is distinctly easy on the ear and timeless in its appeal.

As the label put it, “What has always been uncanny about this music is that it arrives in a state at once familiar and obscured, like a memory weighed down with sensory information but no identifying details to place it. The Wringing Cloth walks off further into that geographical dream without time or language, until it’s just a speck of light….”
items._cn_summary: 这是Old Saw项目的最后一张专辑，由Tongue Depressor成员Henry Birdsey主导，延续美式原音吉他传统，同时融入大量器乐 drone 层叠与磁带噪底。录音在新英格兰多处完成，使用1/4寸磁带，保留模拟质感。编曲以 pedal steel、lap steel 和 resonator 为核心，搭配 nylon 弦吉他、班卓琴、小提琴、簧风琴、电贝斯乃至金属物体与电锤，编制丰富但不喧宾夺主。古典极简主义手法贯穿后半段，铃铛般的高频音刺破 shimmering 的乡村氛围。整体在 Takoma 学派的乡村根源与 drone/ambient 质感之间取得平衡，声音既熟悉又模糊，像一段缺乏辨识细节却充满感官信息的记忆。与用户偏好的实验和暗潮方向有一定距离，但 drone 和极简主义元素提供了一定交集。

items.body:
New LP from mysterious group Ferries on World Of Echo.

"Writing a bio for a secret band is a bit like cleaning a house that nobody is living in. It looks good on your resumé but do we really need it? Only ghosts do.

Talking about ghosts: there is AI for this kind of stuff, but unfortunately, even AI is too serious and will write a 'proper' bio because AI knows stuff. Name names. Name places. Name influences. Name tour dates. Name quotes by Oscar Wilde and/or Noel Gallagher. And none of that is relevant to Ferries.

After the 2025 release of Ferries' quickly-vanishing first LP, Eye Flutter, not much changed for the band. They continued to exist by not existing. Et voila, a new record, Eye Wander, is now here. Although the medium is the same as the previous one (black gold), they've taken a next step in a smoky journey into a dubby and kraut-y world of creating songs and musical moments. Is 'avant garde pop' a genre? Or even 'dub kraut'? I know 'indie' certainly is, and I don't really agree with that either, and even a broken clock is right twice a day so what's the point anyway.

And so - Ferries made a new record called Eye Wander and it is out on World of Echo on 17th July. That's all you need to know for now. - Leon van Barneveld, Bergpolder."
items._cn_summary: Ferries的第二张专辑延续了首作Eye Flutter的神秘路线，由独立小厂World of Echo发行。文章以戏谑口吻拒绝为这支匿名乐队提供任何背景信息，强调音乐本身才是唯一的叙述。相较于首张专辑，新作被描述为向dub和krautrock领域迈进的'烟雾弥漫的旅程'，在节奏循环与驱动式即兴之间寻找新平衡点。作者自创'dub kraut'和'avant garde pop'等临时标签，暗示作品处于类型交叉地带。整体乐评本身更接近概念式的文字游戏而非严肃音乐分析，对音乐具体手法和声音细节几乎没有展开讨论，留给读者自行聆听判断的余地很大。

items.body:
Cold Spring re-issue 'With Extreme Prejudice' by industrial pioneers Sutcliffe Jugend (ex WHITEHOUSE).

"Harsh extreme electronic pioneers Sutcliffe Jugend return with an album of all new material. Three years in the making, and with numerous reworkings, "With Extreme Prejudice" finds Sutcliffe Jugend at the top of their game. Forcing the listener to question their own prejudices and taboos, as modern man struggles to confront and control his inner demons. Musically and lyrically this is SJ's most varied album to date, ranging from harsh electronic onslaughts to a new kind of musical oblivion. Production and sound values are closer to industrial music than ever before, creating a very different feel to their previous filthwork "Pigdaddy". Enter if you dare, the very twisted and real world of Sutcliffe Jugend as they execute With Extreme Prejudice."
items._genre: industrial / harsh noise / power electronics / dark electronic
items._cn_summary: Cold Spring厂牌再版的Sutcliffe Jugend专辑《With Extreme Prejudice》汇集了该工业/极端电子先驱（出身于Whitehouse）的全新录音作品，历时三年反复打磨而成。乐评指出这张专辑在音乐与歌词层面都呈现出此前作品中最丰富的变化幅度，从刺耳的电子轰炸到新型态的音乐虚无感皆有涵盖，制作与声学处理较以往更贴近工业音乐范畴，与前作《Pigdaddy》的低俗质感形成鲜明对比。专辑试图迫使听众审视自身的偏见与禁忌，以极端化的听觉语言映射现代人面对内心阴暗面的挣扎。整体定位介于工业、极端噪音与暗潮电子之间，属于面向特定受众的地下厂牌作品。

items.body:
Back in the game after his ace ‘Poly’ LP helped reboot Ostgut Ton, Efdemin plays true to his minimal techno form on four driving workouts with Dekmantel.

Armed with a refreshed, rugged palette and hunger for tuffer techno, Phillip Sollmann marks some 30 years of fuelling the ‘floor with the ‘Mirror Phase EP’, which escalates in increasingly hard-edged turns from the title tune’s harmonic Berlin-Via-Detroit techno to sludgier acid techno teeming with strange voices in ‘FS1R’, into full Motor City-style flight, a la ‘Landcruising’-era Carl Craig, on ‘Unity Grain’, and the brisk, tweaked-out trot of ’Slip’, which builds to a glorious posh trance peak.
items._genre: minimal techno / acid techno / Detroit techno / electronic
items._cn_summary: Efdemin 在这张EP中回归其minimal techno的根基，呈现四首为舞池服务的硬派techno作品。标题曲以柏林-底特律式的和声质感开场，随后'FS1R'转向更具腐蚀感的acid techno，加入怪异的人声采样；'Unity Grain'则致敬Carl Craig'Landcruising'时期的底特律飞行感；最后一曲'Slip'以快速的碎拍推进，攀升至精致的trance高潮。整体以刷新后的粗粝音色质感为核心，强调功能性舞曲的硬朗质地。Dekmantel作为独立厂牌保持了地下气质，但作品风格偏向俱乐部主流techno路线，实验性与跨界融合元素较为有限。

items.body:
Frisky, trippy hardgroove and techno-trance screwballs from the leading Swede on Local Action’s sexier sibling imprint, b/w Ehua’s fizzing footwork-jungle type remix.

Chasing chops on Blawan’s Voam and a split with Dyslecta for Late Night Shopper in recent years, Mannerfelt is at his kinky, kinetic best here: tweaking out the clean-heeled hardgroove trot and swang of ‘Bubble’ with whirring details under the hood and heart-in-mouth builds, next to the sleeker techno-trance canter of his clipped step and ascendent arps in ‘Iguana Aura’.

For good measure of his range, ‘A Change to Keep I Have’ resets to half-stepped offbeat arranged with the sort of tart, expressive synth tone that fed into his productions on Fever Ray albums, which Ehua duly whisks up into a taut footwork frenzy inflicted with flinty drum funk x neuro D&B bass.
items._cn_summary: 瑞典制作人Peder Mannerfelt在此EP中展现出多变的声音处理能力。A面以尖锐硬派groove为底，'Bubble'在稳定节奏框架内嵌入嗡嗡作响的细节与悬心式渐强；'Iguana Aura'则转向更流畅的技术迷幻路线，以明快的琶音与剪裁感十足的步进节奏推进。B面'A Change to Keep I Have'切换至半步离拍布局，合成器音色带有酸涩而富于表现力的质感，延续了他在Fever Ray专辑中呈现的制作逻辑。Ehua的混音将这首原作重塑为绷紧的footwork狂飙，鼓组锋利，神经质D&B贝斯线穿插其中。整张作品在techno与trance、jungle的边界游走，编曲细节丰富，但对极端实验口味的听众而言仍偏向俱乐部功能而非纯声音探索。

items.body:
Maiden vinyl reissue for a cult 1971 slab of cool and vibrant spiritual jazz by flautist Hadley Caliman and pianist Todd Cochran aka Bayeté, who would go on to play keys/synths for Herbie Hancock, Peter Gabriel, Aretha Franklin.

“Wewantsounds continues its reissue program of Bob Shad's cult jazz label, Mainstream Records, with Hadley Caliman's superb 1972 album, Iapetus. Recorded in LA and featuring a heavyweight lineup of West Coast players including Todd Cochran, Woody “Sonship” Theus, Luis Gasca, and Victor Pantoja, the majority of the album was composed by Todd Cochran (aka Bayeté) soon after he had composed Bobby Hutcherson's Blue Note classic, Head On. A true hidden treasure, it is reissued here on vinyl for the first time since 1971, featuring its original gatefold artwork with rare first-generation photos. This edition comes with newly remastered audio and a two-page insert with exclusive liner notes by Todd Cochran, reflecting on Hadley Caliman and the making of the album.”
items._cn_summary: Hadley Caliman 1971 年专辑《Iapetus》由 Wewantsounds 厂牌再版，原始录制于洛杉矶，是 Mainstream Records 旗下被忽视的精神爵士珍品。专辑以长笛手 Hadley Caliman 为核心，钢琴手 Todd Cochran（又名 Bayeté）贡献了大部分作曲，其余阵容包括 Woody Theus、Luis Gasca、Victor Pantoja 等西海岸乐手。Todd Cochran 在完成 Bobby Hutcherson 经典专辑《Head On》后不久便着手创作了这批作品，乐手阵容之后分别参与了 Herbie Hancock、Peter Gabriel、Aretha Franklin 的录音。此次再版为黑胶首度重制，采用原始折叠封面与初代照片，附 Todd Cochran 亲笔撰写的回忆文字与全新母带处理，呈现七十年代初西海岸爵士即兴传统的鲜活面貌。

A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single �A hist�ria de nossa l�ngua� features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including �Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapu�, Ipanema, Maracan�, Capoeira, etc.� This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer�s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track �Ver meu povo se abra�ar� to the convincing reggae of the second single, �Que seja um reggae�. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, �Independ�ncia� features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings �Battre des ailes� accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on �Dans le sud feat�. The gentle �Strati di tempo� is the closest to Santtana�s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz In�cio Lula da Silva�s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political.� For example, on �L�nguas Gerais,� French rapper Oxmo Puccino �speaks about colonization.� Continuing to quote from the liner notes, �Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.� Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing �Cocanha� in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out.� � Like his popular previous recording O Para�so (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Para�so , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message. Find the artist online.

items._cn_summary: 巴西音乐人Lucas Santtana发行新专辑《Brasiliano》，以多语言音乐探索巴西语言文化的多样性。专辑歌曲涵盖葡萄牙语、法语、英语、西班牙语、奥克语、佛得角克里奥尔语及土著图皮-瓜拉尼语，汇聚不同语言背景的客座词曲作者和演唱者。开篇曲与巴西国宝级音乐人Gilberto Gil合作，以语言拟人化叙事追溯巴西葡萄牙语的历史渊源，融入原住民日常词汇。编曲以手工乐器为主，融合小提琴、钢琴、吉他、键盘与合成器，质感温暖而层次丰富，涵盖派对曲目、雷鬼风格及抒情民谣等多种形态。专辑呈现语言与文化、政治的深层关联，Gil作为前文化部长的参与使作品带有明确的政治立场，跨国合作贯穿始终，是一张关于巴西多元文化身份的温暖音乐宣言。

items._cn_summary: 这是西班牙加泰罗尼亚吉他手 Dani Jané 的第三张专辑，融合弗拉门戈、加泰民间音乐、古典、爵士及探戈等多种元素。专辑以古典组曲结构开篇，结合惠特曼诗歌的西班牙语吟唱与弗拉门戈 bulerías 唱腔。器乐编排以吉他为核心，辅以长笛、安第斯排箫与打击乐，部分曲目加入人声打击与电子音效，呈现细腻的音色对话。歌曲主题多源于家族记忆与故土情感，如致敬祖父1938年诗作的作品和回望童年故居的米隆加。专辑展现了新一代加泰罗尼亚学院派音乐人对弗拉门戈传统的开放态度与跨文化探索。

items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?

items._cn_summary: Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino 庆祝成军五十周年的专辑，通过现任成员重新演绎早期曲目来致敬历史。专辑主要由父子两代音乐人共同完成——老一辈Rina与Daniele Durante创作的标志性曲目《Il Mito》由其子小提琴兼手鼓演奏者Mauro Durante与新一代乐手重新诠释。Roberto Licci与其子Emanuele对唱，早期主唱Rossella Pinto回归演绎经典《Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare》。整体以原声 pizzica 节奏为核心，加入合成贝斯等电子音色点缀，既保留意大利南部传统干燥而富有包裹感的声响，又融入了世界音乐舞台所需的现代编曲层次。专辑还收录与钢琴家 Ludovico Einaudi 合作的《Taranta》remix 版本。制作以家族传承和代际对话为主线，是对一种区域音乐传统全球化进程的回顾与展望。

items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. Further listening: Duo Ruut - Ilmateade Maria Moramarco, Fabio Mina, and Francesco Savoretti - Pietrafonie Jaune Toujours - Vertigo

items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴演奏家Teija Niku的第四张专辑将北欧民谣与巴尔干音乐传统相融合，以手风琴为核心乐器探索跨地域的音乐对话。专辑标题意为'一段模糊的时间'，暗示音乐处于瞬息之间。作品涵盖受保加利亚民间舞蹈节奏启发的欢快曲调、马其顿情歌风格的开阔旋律，以及几首快速的波兰舞曲。整体以北欧感性为基调，巴尔干元素作为色彩点缀。专辑结尾是Niku为已故母亲七十岁生日创作的挽歌，从柔和的抒情过渡到超越性的歌唱段落，情感真挚内敛。评论指出乐手对旋律有敏锐感知，能够在轻快与忧郁、明亮与阴影之间自如转换情绪。

items.body: Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gon�alves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell�s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, �Birthday Song� comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, �I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.� The record closes with �Overture,� anchored by Gon�alves� dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe�s Japanese exhortation, �Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.� Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father�s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. �Snow� begins with Makabe�s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while �Text� swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe�s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe �Morisan� hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music

items._cn_summary: Emi Makabe的第二张专辑以父亲离世为创作核心，将日本传统音乐元素与现代爵士融合。专辑横跨日语演唱、英语吟唱与无词人声，辅以尺八、三味线等传统乐器与钢琴、低音提琴、鼓组的爵士编制。Bill Frisell的客串开场以原声吉他勾勒温暖的情感基调，Jason Moran的钢琴独奏与手风琴穿梭于不同音乐语境之间。专辑尝试在五声音阶传统旋律与bebop摇摆节奏之间建立对话，展现跨文化音乐语汇的交织。作为一位定居纽约的日本音乐人，Makabe以独特的文化视角探索传统与现代的关系，但整体手法更偏向融合而非实验边界探索。

items.body: text:Kenny Inaoka 稲岡邦彌 手元に『打てば響く〜音の力、鍼の力』という本がある。2015年、NHK出版。著者は竹村文近と大友良英。いつ、どこで、どのように入手したのか覚えがない。２年前 (2024年) の12月27日、新宿ピットインで大友良英と山下洋輔、山崎比呂志のトリオのライヴ録音（『Old and New Dreams~Chapter 2 破』DiskUnion) に立ち会った。その時、楽屋で山下さんと大友の間で鍼灸師竹村先生の話題で盛り上がった。竹村先生は二人の共通のかかりつけの鍼灸師で二人のキャリアにとってかけがえのない施術師ということだった。そのとき興味を覚えて買い求めたのかもしれない。 実は筆者も東洋医学の信奉者である。新卒まもなく社用で乗っていたタクシーが日比谷でタクシーと正面衝突、ひどい頚椎捻挫（むち打ち症）を受け、救急病院で１ヶ月半ブロック注射や懸垂などの治療を受けたものの一向に回復せず自主退院、自己判断で東洋医学に切り替えた。自宅近くの老鍼灸師に身を預け、鍼灸と漢方薬を続けること半年、寛解を得たのち完治に至った。最近、おそらくは金属疲労で膝や腰に疼痛を自覚、鍼やマッサージの治療を受けている。盲目の鍼灸師は筆者の質問に対し「鍼を打つことで筋肉の緊張を解いている」と答えた。 さて、著書のタイトル『打てば響く』だが、「反応が早い、理解力が良い」という原意と「鍼や楽器を打手羽効果がある」のダブル・ミーニングであることは容易に察しが付く。大友は永らく重い偏頭痛に悩み、薬も効力を失い演奏にも支障が出るほど。思いあまって山下さんの紹介を受け竹村先生の鍼の治療を受けたところ１回の施術で偏頭痛が嘘のように消えたという。以来定期的な施術を欠かさず度重なる海外ツアーにも耐えているという。著書は、両者のエッセイを随所に含みながら両者の問答を中心に編まれている。 施術の際、竹村先生はいわゆる経絡にこだわるよりも自らの手が動くままに自由に針を打っていくという。経絡の流れは個体差があり、今では患者の身体が鍼を打つべきところを導いてくれる。１回の施術で打つ鍼は平均100本くらい。山下さんコンサートには時々出かけ耳を傾けるが＜ボレロ＞がお気に入り。山下さんに鍼を打つときは＜ボレロ＞のリズムに乗って打つという。ジャズは好きだが大友のライヴにはほとんど行ったことがなく、大友も竹村先生の好みを知っているからあえて声をかけない。施術のBGMはほとんどクラシックだという。ノイズミュージックは施術には合わないことは分かっている。 竹村先生の趣味は高地トレッキング。４、５千メートル級のヒマラヤやアンデスに出かけ、現地で請われるままに鍼を打つ。休暇に出かけても患者を見たら放っては置けない。 山下さんや大友がハード・スケジュールをこなしていけるのも竹村先生の施術の助けがあったようだ。もちろんお二人以外にも有名無名の患者が溢れ、新規の場合には独立した弟子が担当しているそうだ。 なお、著書の中では教えを請うた高柳昌行との確執、独立、劇伴、とくに「あまちゃん」（2013 NHK) の劇伴制作についてなど大友のキャリアの詳細が語られている。ミュージシャンとしての大友良英の生き方、音楽観などを知りたいファンにはぜひ一読をお勧めしたい。初版は10年以上前だが、冒頭に記したように山下さんと大友の竹村先生との関係は２年前に知ったことなので現在でも状況は変わっていないものと思われる。
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评以一本书为引子，围绕针灸师竹村文近与爵士/实验音乐家大友良英、山下洋辅之间的关系展开。书的核心是对谈形式，穿插两位音乐人的随笔，涉及大友永年的偏头痛如何被针灸师一次治愈，以及竹村独特的针法理念——不拘泥于经络，而是让患者身体引导施针位置，平均每次施针约百次。文中还提到竹村在给山下打针时会配合《波莱罗》节奏，以及他本人偏爱古典、对噪音音乐的排斥。评介者结合自身接受针灸治疗的经历，串联起书中关于高柳昌行的分歧、大友独立音乐人之路及NHK剧伴《海女》的制作始末。作为音乐类延伸阅读，适合对山下洋辅和大友良英创作脉络感兴趣的读者。

items.body: Review by arymenezes — This extraordinary box set deserves a comprehensive review. Moreover, purchasing an item of this magnitude is a significant financial decision for many people, so a detailed review can help upon the choice of buying it or not.CD1It's the studio version of "Heavy Horses", with several bonus tracks of demos recorded between 1977 and 1978.Track 1 is dynamic, with good flute and guitar work. The rhythm section is a bit random, with some mismatched time signatures. At the very end, the vocal harmonies are fantastic, and everything fits together very well. Track 2 starts dynamically, then turns into a pop-rock tune with slight folk touches. There's even a brief, well-crafted interlude in the middle, with clapping, flute, and percussion. At the very end, it becomes repetitive. Great guitar intro on the 3rd track, followed by a splendid blues-rock combination involving bass and drums. Good development of the main ideas. Up to 2min, it gains good dynamism and great acceleration. The support of the guitar, even when it's more in the background, is always vigorous and essential. At 4 and a half minutes they return to an inventive blues-rock. This time, with a little more presence of the strings. A good ballad on the 4th track is complemented by a smooth focus on vocal rhythms, performed with a fabulous pitch. The flute phrasing that underlines the vocals also sets the tone for the strings. Enchanting. In the middle there is an efficient interlude. The bass and vocals are somewhat disjointed from each other in the next song. The drums do a good job, but they're also a bit lost. There's no captivating or remotely memorable melody. Furthermore, there's a time signature, quite omnipresent in this composition, that is irritating and simplistic. The strings don't save the main phrases of the 6th track, which are extremely pedantic. But at least they prevent this composition from being even worse. There's a beautiful guitar piece on the 7th track, however everything else is almost childish. The vocals are particularly repetitive and limited. The first half of the 8th track is a mediocre ballad, but are slightly compensated by velvety vocals. From the middle onwards it speeds up a bit, taking on a medieval and concomitantly rock-ish flavor. There's nothing particularly noteworthy, but it's listenable. 10th track offers a strong rhythmic approach, featuring a good blend of cymbals, bass, and strings. Ian's vocals flow with clarity and personality, remaining naturally consistent. The next song is an intricate mix of folk ideas?somewhat raw and slightly disjointed. It could have been a great track had they worked on it a bit more. Track 12 is a good ballad, with beautiful vocal and guitar works. It's almost a copy of one of the acoustic tracks from Aqualung. Doesn't end well. Next song has well-crafted harmonies and a striking looping march. However, it has the same problem as the previous demo regarding the ending, which makes it less memorable than many other Jethro tunes. The guitar contributions on the 14th track are worthwhile, though the choices regarding when to include them were poorly executed. There is a fine interplay between acoustic guitar, flute, and percussion throughout much of this piece of music. The 15th track, "Beltane," is fantastic! It features inventive and amazing vocal harmonies. In fact, everything comes together beautifully and is a delight to the ears. There are some inventive drum patterns and incredible flute "attacks". According to the booklet in the box set, this song was recorded in July 1977 and was intended for the (never-released) 'Moths' EP. It was also considered for the B-side of the "Moths" single, but they ultimately opted for the 1971 track "Life Is a Long Song". The booklet testifies that Beltane first appeared on a release in the 1988 box set '20 Years of Jethro Tull'. Piano and vocals open the 16th track. It is a song with a romantic feel (note: unrelated to the Romantic era). Strings and flute add beautiful contours to the other instruments and also shine when taking the lead in the composition. 17th track: the vocals are expressive, and the acoustic guitar is well forged, without becoming excessive. The flute nicely frames the composition here and there. Strings flow with a sense of youthfulness and elegance. The 18th track is neither good nor bad ? ok, but unremarkable.CD 2In short, both this disc and disc 3 capture a concert performed by JT at the Bern Festhalle in Switzerland on May 28, 1978. Five of the twenty-four tracks from the tapes of this show were used for Bursting Out (with the remaining material sourced from other European concerts). However, as Martin notes in the booklet, Bursting required numerous overdubs to become "presentable". Based on my listening to these CDs of the Swiss show, there are far fewer overdubs here. And the performances are MAGNIFICENT! A listener might complain about songs, regarding his/her personal preferences, but I'd bet high that everyone agrees they're playing at the top of their game!The first track is a classical-style introduction ? albeit with sinister, dramatic touches ? that takes on a playful tone towards the end. Track 2 features a master of ceremonies announcing the show. Track 3 rocks! What chemistry between the guitar and flute! The guitar tones are outstanding, and the drumming is precise, combining economy and power with wonderful artistry. The vitality and sensitivity of all the musicians are immediately apparent. Towards the end, the bass wonderfully drives the track. Track 4 features good guitar riffs, but the rest of the instrumentation doesn't really pop up so high-levelled. It ends in a very loose, unstructured way. Track 5 is a spectacular rendition of the classic "Skating Away on the Thin Ice of the New Day". All the instrumental elements from the original studio version are present, and the bass delivers a magnificent performance, adding a firmer layer of groove. Track 6 is a song I love. The guitar is clear and eloquent. Ian's vocals are incredibly powerful, always remaining fresh and at the right pitch. Well, they didn't perform the entire song, but it's ok, 'cause the quality of the entire presentation is highly remarkable. The harmony of the 7th track initially surprised me, especially for a Heavy Horses song. The music grows in density, transitioning to gentler sections, with good time signatures. The timing of the vocals is less impressive this time. Furthermore, in general, it's a song with slower rhythms, but it lacks the elements that captivate in a slow song. They move on to the title track from the 1978 release. Martin Barre delivers great timbres and marks the notes very well. The rest of the band performs their work perfectly, but what really doesn't help is that the composition is limited. They finished the song very well. On the ninth track, they reach way back to 1969 for a standout blues-rock song from their career: "It Was a New Day Yesterday". With Ian's evolution on the flute, Martin's superb improvement since those early days, and the remaining spectacular lineup, what you hear is nothing short of a powerfull performance. The next track is well-known to Jethro fans, as it appears on Bursting Out. It features a blistering flute solo followed by an exquisite rendition of "God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen/Bourr�e". It speaks for itself; if you haven't heard it yet, give it a listen, dear reader. The eleventh track is a heavier, fully instrumental version of "Living in the Past" blended with "A New Day Yesterday." Unforgettable! The twelfth track features a sublime performance. You can tell the band members are a bit tired, yet they still deliver a beautifully polished gem. After all ? at least to my ears ? "Songs from the Wood" boasts the most exceptional and brilliant vocal harmonies in Tull's entire body of work. Anderson's stamina is impressive, demonstrating such vigor on the flute throughout this sequence of songs (which may not reflect the actual setlist order from the concert, but damn it, it's nice to think it does).CD 3JT always took great care of Thick as a Brick's live performances, and the opening of this disc wasn't different. Therefore, you'll hear 13 minutes of pure delight. They start off brilliantly in Hunting Girl. In fact, they manage to reproduce with accuracy and splendid firmness that truly difficult sequence of bass, guitar, flute, alternating, stopping, returning. Wow, holy gods of musicianship, I was already enchanted when I saw them live here on my city. But in this 1978 recording, they were even several steps above. All the layers and even extra nuances were there, and fortunately, they were recorded and rearranged by the brilliants Steven Wilson and Jakko Jakszyk. They gave Too Old to Rock and Roll, the 3rd track, a slightly naive feel, which was positive, as it gained in fluidity. From the halfway point onwards, the music gains speed, making it even more engaging. The following song, Conundrum, is also on Bursting Out. It's an entirely instrumental experience with a dense sonic mass, based on guitar and drums. A power trio proposal. Intense, but it just lacks a bit of identity. The 5th track has an intense and perfect Minstrel in the Gallery vibe. The guitar is penetrating, and the rock chords paints an impressive sonic density on the whole thing. Besides, Jethro knew very well that shows have to give ROCK AND ROLL to the audience. In the 6th track, the sonic mass is impressive, both in the opening, with extra layers in the instrumental, and also with the unstoppable Martin Barre! To me, it sounds like he is being, in the performance of this song, the inspiration for the others, making everyone, including Anderson, surpass themselves. Shortly after the halfway point, the drummer and bassist seem to think "hey, I'm not going to let the guitarist overshadow me!", and the grow on technique and passion. Exuberant!! The seventh track is a delightful march led by a keyboard-guitar combination. Fantastic. It serves as the prelude to the eighth track, "Aqualung," which kicks off in a truly menacing fashion! The timing is astonishingly good?both regarding the "sluggish" feel of many sections and the transitions between different harmonic structures. They even managed to improve upon the song's conclusion (a part of the original studio version I consider "merely good"). Then comes JT's flagship track, "Locomotive Breath," this time leaning even further into blues and, especially, jazz. When Barre enters, his playing is piercing and deeply inspired! The heavier section of the composition feels even heavier this time ? so much so that the flute gets a bit buried within that dense wall of sound. Right at the end, there is a brief improvisation that serves as a lead-in to the next song, the tenth track: initially a pompous march, it quickly shifts into a vibrant, full-on rock vibe rich with particularly intense nuances. Towards the end, it brilliantly morphs back into a reprise of "Aqualung".DVDsDVD 1 contains the studio album's original stereo mix, as well as Steven Wilson's 5.1 surround remix. I could listen to the former but not the later; I then changed the audio settings, and the sound came through. Therefore, be aware of the sound configuration of your DVD player. Accompanying this audio are images from the studio, the sound engineer, parts of the vinyl liner notes, and footage of instruments, tour travel, backstage moments, etc. As for the difference between the original mix and Mr. Wilson's, he did what is expected of a good engineer: he opened up the instrument separation without sounding excessive. But he didn't do "only" that. On the song "Lullaby", for instance, he turned the bass down slightly and balanced it better with the other instruments so it wouldn't stand out too much?which is what happens in the 1978 version. And on "Journeyman", I noticed right away that the bass is more prominent and has a slightly more metallic tone in this mix. This DVD includes extras, such as a superbly recorded version of the track "Rover" without the string section. There is also another version of "Living in These Hard Times" and the spectacular song "Beltane," which does not appear on the original release of any studio album until 1978.The video content on DVD 2 begins with photos of the 1978 tour. There are duplicated fotos ? some repeated more than once.The video and audio quality of the promotional clips for "Heavy Horses" and "Moths" are exceptional. It is always satisfying to see Ian's wild, boyish face and his almost flamboyant mannerisms. In "Heavy Horses", the whole band appears playing, whereas "Moths" features only the group's leader. The string arrangements on both songs are excellent, although the song about horses feels a bit repetitive to me and could have been shortened. Another bonus video is the promotional (brief, of course) clip for the double album Bursting Out, as well as the short promo video that features both the advertisement for Bursting Out and the announcement of the Madison Square Garden concert.BOOKLETIt contains informationS about the tracks on CD1, original studio credits, dedications, and technical recording details. It also has acknowledgments for the box set edition, as well as additional information regarding the artwork, recording, and production.Drawing on accounts from Ian, Martin, and Dee Palmer (formerly David; the new name was adopted following a gender transition), it also discusses the studio built under Ian's direction ? Maison Rouge ? which, according to its creator, remained in operation for only a few years after the Heavy Horses sessions. The booklet features commentaries ? particularly from these three (former) members ? on the somber atmosphere surrounding the band (and, by extension, the album itself) at the time. Each one of them offers their own theories on the matter, with Dee Palmer's analysis being particularly interesting, including comparisons to the creative and recording processes of other releases. There is also a section dedicated to the numerous demos recorded between 1977 and 1978 (some of which appear as bonus tracks on CD1) and the reasons why they were not ultimately used. So far, I have read 17 of the booklet's 93 pages in full.However, I have leafed through the rest of the content and can say there is a wealth of fascinating information?such as Darryl Way's accounts of his collaborations with JT, details on the UK tour, Ian's recollections regarding each track on Heavy Horses, and a chronology of the era. Last but not least, the song lyrics.About the rating of the box. I don't enjoy Heavy Horses, and that's why I sadly won't give it a 5 stars. My choice is for a 4.8.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评详细解读了Jethro Tull《Heavy Horses》豪华盒装版的CD1内容，包含原专曲目及多首1977-1978年间录制的demo版本。整体呈现为传统民谣摇滚风格融合布鲁斯元素，配以长笛为特色的器乐编排。乐评逐曲分析音轨动态结构、人声旋律走向、和声编排及节奏纹理，指出专辑中部分曲目的时间签名略显随意，部分旋律缺乏记忆点，同时认可长笛独奏、吉他riff与人声和声的精彩段落。作为1978年经典progressive folk专辑的重制版本，盒装以丰富的bonus tracks形式补充了历史录音素材，适合Jethro Tull的忠实粉丝收藏。
